title: Don't ask for the same production twice
statement: Don't ask young learners for the same production twice in one word activity, aloud and then typed; let writing happen once, where it must carry evidence and meaning.
example: One course built a written turn for all 46 taught words and withdrew it the same day.
detail: A Grade 3 reading build added the written vocabulary turn a review asked for, one beat for each of the 46 taught words, gated at 199 assertions, and removed it the same day on the ruling that a word turn should not ask for the same production twice, aloud and typed. The build's BrainLift argues that the repeat spends the child's most expensive minutes on redundancy, since the lesson's typed production already exists in the independent task, where it must carry evidence and meaning, so the vocabulary ladder is hear, then say. The content stays authored, voiced and dormant, held by two gates, so reinstating it is a player change.
against: The review that prompted the turn asked for both: "Have them say the word back, write the word in a sentence," (`grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/archive/g3-reading-v4/FEEDBACK-RESPONSES.md`, line 91), and the build's approval case still lists that ask as decided, not closed.
